title: CLR/103/2013 of Sohan Lal Vs Naveen Chandra AND OTHERS

paras.text:
CLR No. 103 of 2013
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Mr. Mahavir Singh Tyagi, Advocate
for the tenant revisionist.
Mr. T.A. Khan, Senior Advocate
assisted by Mr. Rajesh Joshi, Advocate for
the landlord respondents.
Learned counsel for the revisionist
tenant on the instructions of Mr. Sohan Lal,
who is present before this Court, seeks
permission to withdraw this revision. He,
however, submits that two years time may be
granted to the revisionist tenant to vacate the
shop in question.
On the other hand, Mr. T.A. Khan,
learned Senior Counsel for the landlord,
submits that two years time is on the higher
side and one year time seems to be
appropriate. He, however, submits that this
Court may grant appropriate time to the
tenant revisionist to vacate the disputed shop
on payment of mesne profit at the prevailing
market rate of the rent. According to the
learned counsel for the landlord, prevailing
market rent of the shop, in question, would
be Rs.1500/- p.m.
Learned Trial Court found rate of rent
at Rs. 400/- p.m. The shop was purchased by
the landlord in the year 2005, therefore, it
can very well be said that in the year 2005,
rate of rent was Rs.400/- p.m. In the opinion
of this Court, as on day rent would have
increased to Rs.800/- p.m.
Present petition thus stands disposed
of with the following directions:-
1. Present revision stands
withdrawn on the request of the tenant
revisionist, personally present in the Court.

2. Tenant revisionist shall hand
over peaceful vacant possession of the
disputed shop in question to the landlord
respondent herein on or before 15th
November, 2015.
3. Tenant revisionist shall pay
mesne profit @ Rs.800/- p.m. to the landlord
respondent herein w.e.f. 1st November, 2008
till possession is handed over to the landlord.
Monthly mesne profit shall be paid on or
before 10th day of each and every month.
4. Tenant revisionist shall pay
entire arrears to the landlord respondents on
or before 10th January, 2014 after adjusting
the amount already paid by the tenant, if any.
5. Tenant revisionist shall file an
undertaking to the above effect in the shape
of affidavit before the learned Trial Court on
or before 15th December, 2013.
6. If tenant revisionist makes any
default in the payment of arrears or in the
monthly mesne profit or fails to file
undertaking within time, present revision
shall be deemed to have been dismissed and
revisionist tenant shall be liable to be evicted
forthwith.
7. If tenant revisionist fails to hand
over peaceful vacant actual physical
possession to the landlord of the disputed
shop till 15th November, 2015, landlord shall
be at liberty to evict the tenant revisionist
forthwith at the cost and risk of the tenant.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
Dated 25.11.2013
Shiv
